content:
Feel free to take the credit for my legal updates from now on 😂


New on The HR Vault: download any legal update with your own branding, or your client's, and send it straight on.

If you're an HR consultant, you'll know the routine. A change comes in, you read up on it, then you write it all out again for your clients with your logo at the top.

And the next 12 months look like this:

Third party harassment liability, later this month.

Trade Union stuff, later this month and in January. 

Did you know that unfair dismissal drops to six months from January? No one’s mentioned that to me?! 🥱

The Fair Work Agency taking over minimum wage enforcement, April 2027.

NDA restrictions, sometime in 2027.

Flexible working changes, autumn 2027.

…and I can’t be bothered to list any more, if you want to see them then look here: https://lnkd.in/gEretXFZ

That's before anything else gets announced. (It will 🫠.)

Each one will be in the Vault, ready for your logo.

Pick the update. Pick whose branding. Download it. Send it.

The catch is that I still have to write them. The Employment Rights Act has seen to that until roughly the year 2057.

content:
Good news. Here's an employment law update where nothing has changed yet  🎉 


The governments consultation on workplace monitoring technology closed at 11:59pm on 30 September, and its now going through the responses. 

Here's what was on the table. 

Option A: a statutory Code of Practice. It wouldn't create new duties, but tribunals would take it into account. If you unreasonably failed to follow it, they could adjust compensation by up to 25% in an unfair dismissal or discrimination claim. 

Option B: a legal duty to consult and negotiate with unions, or elected reps where theres no union, before you bring monitoring tech in. With a view to agreement. That one would need primary legislation, so don't hold your breath. 

Option C: guidance. No statutory footing at all. The government also says doing nothing is a legitimate outcome if the evidence doesn't show a problem. 

Bold, given the year we've had. 

Monitoring covers more than you'd think. Door entry systems, vehicle trackers, call recording, keystroke logging, software that scores performance. If it collects information about your staff, its probably in scope. 

In the meantime, UK GDPR hasnt gone anywhere. Anything intrusive already needs a DPIA. 

Have you done yours? Asking for a friend. The friend is the Information Commission. 

Full legal update on The HR Vault here: https://lnkd.in/gGYG_nVY

content:
The government has opened (another) consultation, this time on whistleblowing. It closes on 8 January. 


It's the first proper review of the rules since they came in back in 1999, and the bit employers need to know about is a possible legal duty to have a whistleblowing policy and procedure, and to follow up disclosures.

At the moment that's good practice. This would make it law.

It would apply to private sector employers with 50 or more employees (charities included) and to every public sector employer, whatever the size. Possibly phased in. Civil penalties if you don't comply.

Because if there's one thing employers have been crying out for this year, it's another policy with a legal duty attached.

If it follows the Irish model (the one the consultation sets out in detail), that means a written acknowledgement within 7 days, a designated person to manage disclosures and feedback within 3 months.

The government is very keen to say that following up wouldn't mean formally investigating every disclosure. (I'll believe that when I see the guidance.)

Also on the list: 14 days to apply for interim relief instead of 7, wider protection for groups such as charity trustees, a protected route for telling your trade union and an AI tool to help workers find the right regulator.

Good news. Nothing changes yet, and the response isn't due until 2027.

Which gives me about a year before I rewrite every whistleblowing template in The HR Vault  😁 

Under 50 employees and in the private sector? The duty wouldn't reach you, but whistleblowing protection already does, so don't ditch your policy just yet!

You can read all about it on the legal updates page on The HR Vault here: https://lnkd.in/gd5NCQHh
